text: Broilers are normally left to scavenge to reduce feeding and housing costs, roosting at night wherever they can find shelter, including in trees. A simple night shelter with perches protects them from predators like stray dogs and allows manure to be collected for use as fertilizer; fencing broilers within a limited area is generally more realistic for village farmers than fully confining them, since full confinement requires the farmer to provide all feed. Free-ranging poultry carry disease transmission risk (Salmonella, Pasteurella) from dirty environments as well as predator risk. Fencing a limited area lets the farmer distribute only complementary feed, keeps hygiene easier to maintain (no stray plastic bags or dirty puddles), reduces contact with other scavenging or possibly sick poultry, and keeps children away from areas soiled with droppings.
